questions.prompt: What distinguishes a stateful firewall from a stateless one?

options.text: It tracks connections and automatically allows replies to permitted flows
It encrypts all traffic that passes through
It judges each packet in isolation with no memory

questions.explanation: A stateful firewall keeps a connection-tracking table and allows established/related replies. Judging each packet alone describes a stateless filter.

questions.prompt: Which is the safer default firewall posture?

options.text: Default-deny: block all, allow only what's needed
Default-allow: permit all, block only known-bad
Allow all inbound, deny all outbound

questions.explanation: Default-deny (allow-list) exposes only explicitly needed traffic; default-allow inevitably leaves gaps as services and threats change.

questions.prompt: Firewall rules are usually evaluated top-to-bottom with ____-match wins, ending in a catch-all deny.
questions.explanation: First-match-wins means a broad deny placed above a needed allow will block it; put specific allows before the catch-all deny.

questions.prompt: Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

options.text: A host-based firewall protects a single machine
A firewall cannot stop attacks inside traffic it deliberately allows
Reducing attack surface means closing unused ports and services
A firewall alone is complete security with no other controls needed

questions.explanation: Host firewalls protect one machine, firewalls can't police allowed-service vulnerabilities, and closing ports reduces surface. Security needs defense in depth, not a firewall alone.

questions.prompt: Order these firewall rules correctly for a default-deny inbound policy on a web server.
questions.explanation: Specific allows and the established/related rule must come before the catch-all deny, or first-match would block them.

questions.prompt: Match each term to its meaning.

pairs.right: The set of exposed services an attacker could target
Block all, allow only what's needed
Replies to a permitted outbound connection

questions.explanation: Attack surface is what's exposed, defense in depth layers controls, default-deny is an allow-list posture, and established/related covers tracked replies.
